criteria.text: Treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) or progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) in adults.
Patient is at least 18 years old (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a pulmonologist (approval criterion 2).
Other known causes of interstitial lung disease, including environmental exposure, drug toxicity and connective tissue disease, ruled out (approval criterion 3).
Documented pulmonary function test within the past 60 days shows FVC ≥45% predicted (approval criterion 4).
Baseline DLCO, corrected for hemoglobin, ≥25% predicted (approval criterion 5).
IPF confirmed by lung biopsy OR high-resolution computed tomography (approval criterion 6).
PPF diagnosis consistent with current, established guidelines (approval criterion 7).
Jascayd is not used in combination with a moderate or strong CYP3A inducer (denial criterion 2).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Jascayd (nerandomilast) Criteria Version 1: Original 12/19/2025; Accepted 01/16/2026; Effective 03/01/2026.

Encoded: two closed indications, shared approval criteria 1–5, indication-specific confirmation criteria 6–7, and denial criterion 2. Denial criterion 1 (failure to meet approval criteria) is represented by approval clauses. Clinical documentation attestations require manual review.
Cautions (notes only): dose modification may be necessary with concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors; diarrhea was the most commonly reported side effect.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to one year.
Quantity limit (notes only): 60 tablets per 30 days. Numeric quantity enforcement is not encoded.

Documentation verification, monitoring, duration, reauthorization and quantity limits require manual review. Ofev and Esbriet are alternatives subject to their own indication and eligibility criteria.
